tasks.title: write_targets calls read-only paths writes, so it refuses good commands
tasks.why: P1. relay_hook.py write_targets (203-234) collects paths a command only READS and hands each to off_limits (279-282), which then refuses the call. Run against integration's own code: `python -c "import json;d=json.load(open(r'<board>/relay/queue/u1.json'));open('out.txt','w').write(...)"` yields the board queue path, because the CODE_WRITE branch (228-234) takes every quoted token out of any word that holds a write verb anywhere, so the one path the code reads is refused with 'on the board a leg writes only under evidence/'. `python x.py < <board>/relay/queue/u1.json` yields that path too, because redirects() returns input redirects as well (cmdrules.py:259-270) and line 215 keeps whatever follows the last < or >. `cp <relay-run>/Tools/relay/runner.py /tmp/r.py` yields the SOURCE file (222-227 takes every non-flag argument of a WRITE_PROGS program), refused with 'a leg does not edit the relay or the pipeline tools'; `tar -czf out.tgz <...>/Tools/relay` is the same. A commit message is caught as well: `relay.py leg finish -m "... <abs path under Tools/relay> ... rename ..."` yields that path, so a leg's close-out can be refused over its own message. pre-tool fails closed and the leg is told not to retry (_common.md), so each of these ends a leg's step or its close-out for a read. Fix: take a path only from an output redirect, from an argument in a write position, and from a token the write call itself names; never from a plain read.

The new cases are red on today's relay_hook.py.

tasks.title: One unreadable queue file still kills the whole lane queue
tasks.why: P2. sources/lane.py next():96-99 now catches FileNotFoundError, but load() (35-58) raises SystemExit for a file that is not valid JSON or is missing a field, and lets OSError/PermissionError out of read_json untouched. Either escapes next(), and run_units catches it at runner.py:701 as 'error: ...', so the run stops with no unit taken: every later unit in the queue waits for a person, which is the failure the FileNotFoundError fix was for. files():81-85 already treats both as survivable when it sorts the queue ('a file that cannot be read sorts as one with no priority'), so the two halves of the same module disagree. The loud SystemExit for bad JSON is on purpose for a file the owner just queued, but it costs every other unit in the queue, and an OSError (a file held open while the board syncs on Windows) is nobody's mistake at all. Fix: catch OSError and SystemExit around load() in next(), print which file and why, and go on to the next unit.

tasks.title: off_limits resolves a relative write path against the hook's own cwd
tasks.why: P2. The new check (relay_hook.py:279-282) feeds write_targets' words to off_limits, which compares them with inside()/cmdrules.norm_path (74-86). norm_path calls os.path.realpath, so a relative word is made absolute against the HOOK PROCESS's working directory, and the hook is never told the leg's: leg.json carries desk, board and work, but refusal() passes the word through as it stands. Two wrong answers follow from the same line. A write the leg aims at a forbidden place with a relative path (`cd <somewhere> && echo x > ../relay/queue/u.json`, or any command after a cd) is measured from the wrong folder and let through; and a harmless relative word under a leg whose cwd is not the hook's can land inside the board or the runner's folder once realpath is done with it and be refused for nothing. Fix: judge only paths that are already absolute, or resolve a relative one against leg['work'] and say so in the docstring; either way one rule, not the process's accident.
tasks.done_when: A new case in test_relay.py that runs relay_hook.refusal with the process cwd set to a folder inside the fake board: a Bash command writing to a plain relative file (`echo x > out.txt`) is let through, and one writing to a relative path that reaches the board's queue is denied, with the same answers whatever the process cwd is. Red on today's relay_hook.py, where both answers follow the cwd; `python Tools/relay/test_relay.py Guard` exits 0.

tasks.title: Two docs still say the push hook allows only a forward push
tasks.why: P3. prepush.py's ancestor check went when the owner's 2026-10-18 row let a leg force-push its own lane, and prepush.py's own docstring (2-3) and roles/_common.md say 'forward or forced'. Two pages still say the old rule: docs/reference/relay.md:472 ('refuses every push from it except a forward push of the leg's own lane') and docs/reference/pipelines.md:271 ('only a forward push of its own lane leaves it'). validate.py cannot read prose, so nothing catches it. A leg or a session that reads either page believes a rebased lane cannot be pushed and ends BLOCKED on a push that now works, which is exactly the waste the 2026-10-18 decision was taken to end (decisions.md:429-447 lists two lanes that cost the owner a hand push).
